name: claude-auto-switch
description: Auto switch your Claude accounts; Claude Code uses the one whose limit resets soonest, with live usage limits.

commands.title: Claude: Save current account as profile
Claude: Refresh accounts, current login and limits
Claude: Log in from terminal (replaces the current account)
Claude: Switch to the next account now (auto-switch)
Claude: Set an account's auto-switch hand-over limit
Claude: Keep an account active (pause auto-switching)
Claude: Include or exclude an account in auto-switching
Claude: Back up account list (password-protected ZIP)
Claude: Restore account list from backup

claudeAutoSwitch.autoRefresh.markdownDescription: Regularly check the usage limits of all saved accounts (every `#claudeAutoSwitch.pollIntervalSeconds#` seconds). When disabled, usage is only checked at startup, on manual refresh, and when a used-up limit is due to reset.

claudeAutoSwitch.pollIntervalSeconds.markdownDescription: How often (in seconds, minimum 60 = 1 minute) to check usage limits for each account when `#claudeAutoSwitch.autoRefresh#` is on. The usage endpoint is rate-limited: short intervals with many accounts can hit HTTP 429, after which that account is paused for 5 minutes.

claudeAutoSwitch.requestDelaySeconds.markdownDescription: Pause (in seconds) between requests to Anthropic. Accounts are checked one at a time, never in parallel, with this pause in between, so checking many accounts does not hit the rate limit (HTTP 429). Raise it if you still see 429 errors.

claudeAutoSwitch.notifyOnLimitReset.markdownDescription: Show a notification when a used-up limit (session, weekly, or a model-specific weekly limit) of a saved account becomes available again.

claudeAutoSwitch.warnThresholdPercent.markdownDescription: Usage threshold (%) from which limit bars and the status bar turn red. They turn orange from 75% of it (60% by default).

claudeAutoSwitch.autoSaveNewAccounts.markdownDescription: Save a Claude Code login as an account as soon as it appears, so logging in is all you have to do. When off, the panel offers a **Save** button instead.

claudeAutoSwitch.manualSwitchHoldMinutes.markdownDescription: How long (in minutes) an account you switch to by hand is held before auto-switching may move again. The hold ends early if the account runs out of a limit. `0` turns it off, so the next round can switch straight back; the ★ button holds an account indefinitely.

claudeAutoSwitch.autoReloadAfterSwitch.markdownDescription: Automatically reload the VS Code window after switching accounts (required for Claude Code to pick up the new account). When disabled, the extension asks first.

claudeAutoSwitch.autoSwitch.enabled.markdownDescription: Switch to the next account on its own as soon as the active account runs out of a limit (and when a better account becomes available). The next account is chosen by `#claudeAutoSwitch.autoSwitch.order#`; every saved account takes part unless it is excluded from the panel's **⋯** menu.

enumDescriptions: Keep the account that `#claudeAutoSwitch.autoSwitch.order#` puts first active, so the capacity that resets soonest is the one being spent. Switches as soon as another account takes that place.
Switch only when the active account runs out of a limit, and stay on it as long as it can be used.
claudeAutoSwitch.autoSwitch.when.markdownDescription: When auto-switching moves to another account.

enumDescriptions: The account whose weekly (7-day) limit resets soonest goes first, so its capacity is used before it is lost.
The account whose next limit of any kind resets soonest goes first.
The account that would lose the most capacity per hour goes first.
The account with the most usage left goes first.
The first available account in the panel's order goes first.
claudeAutoSwitch.autoSwitch.order.markdownDescription: The order in which available accounts are taken by auto-switching.

claudeAutoSwitch.autoSwitch.minAvailable.markdownDescription: An account is only switched to when at least this much (%) of every one of its limits is left.

claudeAutoSwitch.autoSwitch.notify.markdownDescription: Show a notification naming the account auto-switching moved to, and why.

claudeAutoSwitch.autoSwitch.sortList.markdownDescription: Sort the accounts panel by `#claudeAutoSwitch.autoSwitch.order#`, so the account that is used next is at the top. Choosing a sort in the panel overrides this.

claudeAutoSwitch.usageHistory.enabled.markdownDescription: Collect a usage reading of every saved account every `#claudeAutoSwitch.usageHistory.intervalSeconds#` seconds and keep it on this computer, for the usage analytics charts and the availability calendar. Readings that repeat the previous values are not stored again (except every 15 minutes).

claudeAutoSwitch.usageHistory.intervalSe.markdownDescription: How often (in seconds, minimum 60) usage is read while `#claudeAutoSwitch.usageHistory.enabled#` is on. Short periods with many accounts can hit the usage endpoint's rate limit (HTTP 429), which pauses that account for 5 minutes.

claudeAutoSwitch.usageHistory.retentionD.markdownDescription: How many days of collected usage history to keep.

claudeAutoSwitch.credentialsPath.markdownDescription: Path to the Claude Code `.credentials.json` file. Empty = default `~/.claude/.credentials.json`. On macOS, Claude Code keeps the login in the Keychain instead; this path's folder selects which Keychain item is used.

claudeAutoSwitch.claudeCommand.markdownDescription: Claude Code CLI command used for login and Say Hi warmups. Use the full path to `claude.cmd`/`claude.exe` if VS Code cannot find `claude` in PATH.

claudeAutoSwitch.sayHiModel.markdownDescription: Model passed to `claude -p` for Say Hi warmups. `haiku` is the low-cost/default warmup choice.

claudeAutoSwitch.sayHiPrompt.markdownDescription: Prompt used by Say Hi warmups.

claudeAutoSwitch.sayHiTimeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: Maximum time to wait for a Say Hi warmup command.
